body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. We imported CAMCraft’s five-sided punches and ran FORMALCHECK and GRAFICHECK. The plotted paths followed all five faces at the four expected outward offsets. The control preserved the threading point and the 1 mm separation on the oblique face.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

The target parent for this draft is the corrected #2951 at `f92e67857`. Its trial merge with `6b790f4dd` conflicts in `crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie/tests.rs` and `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`.

The two versions change how the post prepares the contour. The parent builds a guarded punch setup with checked stock and threading coordinates. This draft extends the earlier preparation code to split an oblique entry face and check corner clearance. Taking either version as a whole would lose required behavior.

Our proposed update keeps the parent's zero-step setup and ports the oblique entry, face-split and corner checks into it. The combined tests must check both the nominal path and the refusal cases. A fresh offline control import must show the oblique path and zero working steps. The earlier four-pass control plot applies to the previous writer.

The draft remains on its current head for individual review after #2951.

Port onto `main` is pushed. The head is `9787bf79e`. It merges cleanly with `main` at `09ad779ee`.

What the port did:
- It merged `main` into the branch (no rebase, no force-push). The conflicts were in `crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie/tests.rs` and `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`.
- It used the files of `main` as the frame. The zero-step `PunchSetup20` setup of #2984, the checked stock and start hole, and the 1.0 mm separation rule stay as they are on `main`.
- It ported the convex envelope check, the oblique entry search, the exterior grid seam and the corner-clearance check into `prepare()`. They replace only the rectangle refusal and the old entry search.
- The old writer of this branch is not used. The rectangular output stays byte for byte the same.
- Refusal texts name the problem, not the machine (#3537). The examples use the post name "Native wire EDM job files".
- A new test, `oblique_punch_posts_the_zero_step_setup_and_its_faces`, posts the oblique punch through `export_with_review`. It checks the full ISO file, the zero-step SBL fields and the refusal of separation 0.0.
- A second commit removes a clippy finding. The NaN check stays.

Gate: quick 11 of 11 steps green (103 `camcraft-post` lib tests, 69 `camcraft-app` tests). `agie_native`, `mcp_wire_contour` and `mcp_doc_drift` are green. Clippy on `camcraft-post` is clean. The PR body has the readings.

Owed by the author: a fresh offline control import of `POLY20` and `SLOPE20` on the control VM. The earlier control plots used the old writer of this branch. They do not apply to the ported writer. The import must show the oblique path and zero working steps.

The PR also changes the `camcraft-mcp` skill row. The body has `Process change: yes`.

## Offline control import: POLY20 and SLOPE20 (2026-11-23)

The jobs came from head `30e6c4c3f` (the port stack #2955, #2964, #2968, #2969). This head contains the head `9787bf79e` of this PR. The CLI ran `examples/agie/oblique-punch.camscript` and `examples/agie/slope-punch.camscript` without changes. Each receipt says `"working_steps_generated": false`.

### Procedure

- Emulated AGIEVISION CUT Classic S. A throwaway clone of the saved state `practice-color-ready`. The state was reloaded before each job, so no job saw an earlier import.
- Import of the ISO into `ISO Sys`, then the SBL with its SBR into `SBL Sys`, from a read-only floppy image.
- A host-side read of the guest disk confirmed that the imported ISO and SBL bytes are equal to the CamCraft files.
- New piece from `Script Files`. FORMALCHECK with and without warnings. TECCUT assignment. GRAFICHECK. The plot file `1.J00` was copied out and read.

### Readings

| Reading | POLY20 | SLOPE20 |
|---|---|---|
| Work line after import | `CUT1 - CCB030[0]` | `CUT1 - CCB030[0]` |
| FORMALCHECK before TECCUT | one error: `Technologie : te definiëren` (expected for zero steps) | the same |
| TECCUT header | `Dia:0.25 H:20 Ra:0.30 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5`, Mat Fe, Maf BC | the same |
| Pre-selected row | `0199 01.36 4`, technology `estbca25nnn060b030020` | the same |
| Work line after TECCUT | `CCB030[4]` (Main, Trim1, Trim2, Trim3) | `CCB030[4]` |
| Pass offsets (µm) | 245, 155, 140, 134 | 245, 155, 140, 134 |
| FORMALCHECK after TECCUT | `Controleresultaat: geen fouten.` | the same |
| Warnings after TECCUT | `Uitgekozen opties : 131072`, `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` | the same |

The TECCUT header agrees with the CamCraft receipt: Berco Cut 0.25, 20 mm, CCB030 with Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.00 and Te 1.50.

### Plot (`1.J00`)

POLY20:
- Start hole X-20.5 Y6, diameter 2.0.
- The rough pass follows the five nominal faces at 0.245 mm: Y-10.245 on the bottom face, X22.196 Y-2.147 and X22.232 Y-1.923 at the oblique corner, Y10.245 on the top face. The convex corners have arcs of the offset radius.
- The entry is on the oblique face, at the foot X-12.5 Y0.
- The control stops the main loop at X-12.096 Y0.947 and leaves a separation from X-12.696 Y0.147. This length is 1.000 mm along the oblique face.
- Trim1, Trim2 and Trim3 are on the same faces at 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. Each pass returns to X-20.5 Y6.
- The separation section then cuts the 1 mm with Main and the three trims.

SLOPE20:
- The entry is on the exterior grid point X-12.64765 Y0.50336 on the oblique face.
- The rough pass stops at X-12.2749 Y1.4631 and leaves a separation from X-12.8484 Y0.6439. This length is 1.000 mm.
- Offsets and faces are as for POLY20. Each pass returns to X-20.5 Y6.

### Result

Both jobs agree with the expectation: the oblique path, zero working steps at import, the measured 20 mm offsets after TECCUT, and no FORMALCHECK error after TECCUT. I found no mismatch.

### Not checked

- No physical cut.
- Screenshots and the `.J00` files are in the local notes folder `agie-imports-20261123/POLY20` and `agie-imports-20261123/SLOPE20`. They are not attached here.

Reply to the review of 9787bf79e (item 1, the control check).

The fresh offline control import of POLY20 and SLOPE20 from the ported writer is complete. The results are in [this comment](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2955#issuecomment-7115464026). The jobs came from head 30e6c4c3f of the port stack. That head contains this PR head, and the posted job files for these two jobs do not depend on the PRs above this one.

- Zero erosion steps after import: CCB030[0].
- Assigned technology: the pre-selected TECCUT row matched the receipt (Dia 0.25, H 20, Ra 0.30). After TECCUT the work showed CCB030[4].
- Retained side: punch.
- FORMALCHECK after TECCUT: Controleresultaat: geen fouten.
- GRAFICHECK: POLY20 has 5 nominal faces and the entry on the oblique face at X-12.5 Y0. SLOPE20 has the entry at X-12.64765 Y0.50336. Both have a 1.000 mm separation and a return to the start hole.

The PR body now refers to these results. The head is unchanged at 9787bf79e. Ready for a re-check.
